Claude Certified Architect
[[unofficial]] prep kit
scenes.subtitle: Study guide PDF · Mock exams PDF · Practice app (.exe)

lines.say: Are you preparing for the Claude Certified Architect, Foundations exam, and wondering where to start?
In this video, I'm sharing three free files to help you prepare: a study guide in PDF, a mock exam workbook in PDF, and a Windows practice app.
But first, one important note.

lines.say: These files are not official, and they are not provided by Anthropic.
They are independent study material. Anthropic did not make them, review them, or endorse them.
The questions are original practice questions, written to match the published exam domains. They are not real exam questions.
And exam details, like the format or the pass mark, can change. So always confirm them on the official exam page before you book.

scenes.banner: 5 domains: agents · tools & MCP · Claude Code · prompts · context

lines.say: Here's what the exam looks like, based on the published exam guide.
Sixty multiple-choice questions in two hours. That's about two minutes per question.
Every question sits inside a realistic production scenario. You get four scenarios, drawn from a bank of six.
Scores are scaled from 100 to 1,000, and the pass mark is 720.
lines.tts: Scores are scaled from one hundred to one thousand, and the pass mark is seven hundred and twenty.

lines.say: The questions cover five domains: agent architecture, tool design and MCP, Claude Code, prompt engineering, and context management.

cards.title: Study guide (PDF)
cards.text: 57 pages: every domain, explained for beginners

cards.title: Practice app (.exe)
cards.text: The same 10 exams · practice & timed modes

lines.say: You get three files.
A fifty-seven page study guide that teaches every domain.
A printable mock exam workbook: ten exams, two hundred questions, with full answer keys.
And a Windows practice app, with the same ten exams, in practice and timed modes.
Let's start with the study guide.
It's written for beginners. Chapter zero explains the exam, and chapter one covers the basics, like what an API call and a tool are.
Then there's one chapter per domain, so you can see exactly how much each one is worth.
Each chapter explains the ideas with real code, annotated line by line, like this agent loop.
Inside, you'll find comparison tables, like the workflow patterns and when to use each one.
Diagrams, like this coordinator and its subagents.
And real configuration files for Claude Code, such as permission rules and hooks.
Every chapter ends with a lab exercise and a short quiz. Later chapters solve all six exam scenarios, and finish with a four-week study plan and a glossary.
The second file is the mock exam workbook: ten exams in a ninety-six page PDF, from Foundation level up to exam level.
Each exam has twenty questions grouped under their scenario, like on the real exam, and an answer sheet you can print.
After each exam, the answer key explains the correct answer and why every other option is wrong.
At the end, a score table and a master answer grid help you track all ten attempts.

scenes.heading: One click to start
scenes.label: CCA-F_Mock_Exams.exe
points: Opens the **practice app** in its own window

lines.say: The third file is the Windows app. It's a single file, so there's nothing to install.
Double-click it, and choose Start the practice app. It opens in its own window.
You can also open the mock exam workbook from here.
Everything is bundled inside, so it works offline too.
Windows may warn you the first time, because the file isn't signed. Choose More info, then Run anyway.
This is the practice app. It's where you'll spend most of your time.
The home page sums up the exam format.
And the five domain weights, so you know where to focus.
Below, you'll find the ten mock exams. Each one has twenty questions across four scenarios.
Every exam has two modes: Practice, and Timed.

scenes.heading: Practice mode: learn from every answer
scenes.label: Mock Exam 1 · Practice

lines.say: In practice mode, you pick an answer and check it right away.
Here, I chose A on purpose. The app marks it wrong, and tells me why it's wrong.
It highlights the correct answer.
And explains the reasoning behind it. Every wrong option has its own note too, because understanding the traps is how you pass a scenario exam.
Timed mode puts you under exam conditions.
You get two minutes per question, so forty minutes for the whole exam.
You can flag a question, move on, and come back to it later from the navigator, just as you would on exam day.
When you finish, you get your score and an estimated scaled score. It's a simple estimate, not the official formula.
You also see your score in each domain, so your weak spots are obvious.
And you can review every question you missed, with your answer, the correct one, and the explanation.
Your best score for each exam is saved, so you can track your progress.

scenes.chapter: How to study with the files
scenes.heading: How to [[study]] with them

cards.title: Learn
cards.text: Read one domain chapter at a time and do its lab

cards.title: Test: exams 6–10
cards.text: Timed mode. No notes, 40 minutes each

cards.title: Review
cards.text: Re-read your misses. Aim for 16/20 before booking

lines.say: So, how should you use them?
First, learn. Read the study guide one domain at a time, and do the lab at the end of each chapter.
Then practise with exams one to five, in practice mode. Read every explanation, even when you're right.
Next, test yourself with exams six to ten in timed mode. No notes, forty minutes each.
Finally, review your misses. Aim for sixteen out of twenty, or better, before you book the real exam.
